final_answer: antibiotic resistance arises from natural selection acting on bacterial populations. when antibiotics are used, they kill most bacteria, but a few may already possess mutations or acquired genes that confer resistance (e.g., enzymes that inactivate the drug, altered target sites, efflux pumps). these resistant bacteria survive, reproduce, and pass on their resistance traits. overprescription accelerates this by increasing selective pressure: more antibiotics are used, killing susceptible strains and allowing resistant ones to dominate. repeated or inappropriate use also promotes the spread of resistance genes via horizontal gene transfer (plasmids, transposons) and reduces the time for resistant variants to emerge and propagate.
